name: DataAvailabilityHeader

fields.name: column_roots
fields.comment: ColumnRoot_j = root((M_{1,j} || M_{2,j} || ... || M_{2k,j} ))

comment:
DataAvailabilityHeader contains the row and column roots of the erasure
 coded version of the data in Block.Data.
 Therefore the original Block.Data is arranged in a
 k × k matrix, which is then "extended" to a
 2k × 2k matrix applying multiple times Reed-Solomon encoding.
 For details see Section 5.2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.09044
 or the Celestia specification:
 https://github.com/celestiaorg/celestia-specs/blob/master/src/specs/data_structures.md#availabledataheader
 Note that currently we list row and column roots in separate fields
 (different from the spec).

name: NMTProof

fields.name: start
fields.comment: Start index of this proof.

fields.name: end
fields.comment: End index of this proof.

fields.name: nodes
fields.comment:
Nodes that together with the corresponding leaf values can be used to
 recompute the root and verify this proof. Nodes should consist of the max
 and min namespaces along with the actual hash, resulting in each being 48
 bytes each

fields.name: leaf_hash
fields.comment:
leafHash are nil if the namespace is present in the NMT. In case the
 namespace to be proved is in the min/max range of the tree but absent, this
 will contain the leaf hash necessary to verify the proof of absence. Leaf
 hashes should consist of the namespace along with the actual hash,
 resulting 40 bytes total.

comment:
NMTProof is a proof of a namespace.ID in an NMT.
 In case this proof proves the absence of a namespace.ID
 in a tree it also contains the leaf hashes of the range
 where that namespace would be.

ShareProof is an NMT proof that a set of shares exist in a set of rows and a
 Merkle proof that those rows exist in a Merkle tree with a given data root.

name: InterfaceDescriptor

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
name is the name of the interface. It should be a short-name (without
 a period) such that the fully qualified name of the interface will be
 package.name, ex. for the package a.b and interface named C, the
 fully-qualified name will be a.b.C.

fields.name: description
fields.comment:
description is a human-readable description of the interface and its
 purpose.

comment:
InterfaceDescriptor describes an interface type to be used with
 accepts_interface and implements_interface and declared by declare_interface.

name: ScalarDescriptor

fields.name: name
fields.comment:
name is the name of the scalar. It should be a short-name (without
 a period) such that the fully qualified name of the scalar will be
 package.name, ex. for the package a.b and scalar named C, the
 fully-qualified name will be a.b.C.

fields.name: description
fields.comment:
description is a human-readable description of the scalar and its
 encoding format. For instance a big integer or decimal scalar should
 specify precisely the expected encoding format.

fields.name: field_type
fields.comment:
field_type is the type of field with which this scalar can be used.
 Scalars can be used with one and only one type of field so that
 encoding standards and simple and clear. Currently only string and
 bytes fields are supported for scalars.

comment:
ScalarDescriptor describes an scalar type to be used with
 the scalar field option and declared by declare_scalar.
 Scalars extend simple protobuf built-in types with additional
 syntax and semantics, for instance to represent big integers.
 Scalars should ideally define an encoding such that there is only one
 valid syntactical representation for a given semantic meaning,
 i.e. the encoding should be deterministic.

name: PageRequest

fields.name: key
fields.comment:
key is a value returned in PageResponse.next_key to begin
 querying the next page most efficiently. Only one of offset or key
 should be set.

fields.name: offset
fields.comment:
offset is a numeric offset that can be used when key is unavailable.
 It is less efficient than using key. Only one of offset or key should
 be set.

fields.name: limit
fields.comment:
limit is the total number of results to be returned in the result page.
 If left empty it will default to a value to be set by each app.

fields.name: count_total
fields.comment:
count_total is set to true  to indicate that the result set should include
 a count of the total number of items available for pagination in UIs.
 count_total is only respected when offset is used. It is ignored when key
 is set.

fields.name: reverse
fields.comment:
reverse is set to true if results are to be returned in the descending order.

 Since: cosmos-sdk 0.43

name: PageResponse

fields.name: next_key
fields.comment:
next_key is the key to be passed to PageRequest.key to
 query the next page most efficiently. It will be empty if
 there are no more results.

fields.name: total
fields.comment:
total is total number of results available if PageRequest.count_total
 was set, its value is undefined otherwise

name: Coin
comment:
Coin defines a token with a denomination and an amount.

 NOTE: The amount field is an Int which implements the custom method
 signatures required by gogoproto.

name: DecCoin
comment:
DecCoin defines a token with a denomination and a decimal amount.

 NOTE: The amount field is an Dec which implements the custom method
 signatures required by gogoproto.

name: PrivKey
comment: PrivKey defines a secp256k1 private key.

name: PubKey
comment:
PubKey defines a secp256k1 public key
 Key is the compressed form of the pubkey. The first byte depends is a 0x02 byte
 if the y-coordinate is the lexicographically largest of the two associated with
 the x-coordinate. Otherwise the first byte is a 0x03.
 This prefix is followed with the x-coordinate.
